solution: True. India's position in Asia is geographically and politically important. India is the biggest country in the Indian subcontinent, and is also economically and technologically more advanced. It is therefore natural that India has a great influence among the South Asian countries. India has established relations with all her neighbours on the basis of equality and mutual respect, which are values of great importance in India's foreign policy.

False. This chapter describes the India-China relationship as one of conflict and concern, not of friendship. The conflict is connected to two issues: the border dispute over the Aksai Chin area and the Macmahon Line, and the status of Tibet. China claims that the area south of Aksai Chin and the Macmahon Line, that is Arunachal Pradesh, is Chinese territory and is not willing to agree that the Macmahon Line is an international border, and in 1962 China attacked India. Tibet was traditionally autonomous, but when China was stepping up its military control there the Dalai Lama took asylum in India, and this issue too has been responsible for conflict between the two countries. The friendship between China and Pakistan, the supply of weapons from China to Pakistan, the transfer of missile and nuclear weapons technology, and China's increasing influence over India's other neighbours are a cause of concern for India. India has always made efforts to improve relations - a joint executive group has been set up for the border dispute, trade relations have strengthened as both economies grew, and tripartite talks between Russia, China and India have been held - and the chapter says that because of this Sino-Indian relations are improving slowly and the border dispute has taken a back seat. But the chapter says only that these relations are improving slowly; it nowhere calls them friendly, so the statement is false.

True. After 1985 there was political instability in Sri Lanka as a result of the differences between the Tamils and the Sri Lankan Government. At that time India sent a peacekeeping force to help the Sri Lankan government. India has friendly relations with her southern neighbour Sri Lanka, and these friendly relations are important from the point of view of security in the Indian Ocean.

The chapter also names the Tashkent Agreement of 1966 between India and Pakistan, so row 1 may be answered with that agreement as well.

The Shimla Agreement was made between India and Pakistan in 1972. It was based on the Indian world view, which opposed the military alliances of the Cold War and tried to solve the Indo-Pak conflict bilaterally, that is, between the two countries themselves. It came after the war of 1971, which was about the creation of Bangladesh but also had the dimension of the Kashmir problem to it. The Shimla Agreement provided a new format to the interaction between India and Pakistan.

The foundation of the friendship between India and Nepal was laid with the Indo-Nepalese Friendship Treaty in 1950. According to this treaty, Nepalese citizens can not only enter India, but are also permitted to take up government jobs and carry on trade in India. Nepal is a landlocked country surrounded by mountainous terrain, and its boundaries are linked with India and China. Nepal is dependent upon India for economic progress, basic facilities, food related needs, trade and energy needs.

The Macmahon Line is one of the two areas of the border dispute between India and China, the other being the Aksai Chin area. China claims that the area lying to the south of Aksai Chin and the Macmahon Line, that is Arunachal Pradesh, is Chinese territory, and China is not willing to agree that the Macmahon Line is an international border. India has made several efforts to sort out this border dispute by means of dialogue, but has not met with much success. A joint executive group has been set up to solve the Sino-Indian border dispute.
[Note: the chapter does not state when, by whom or on what basis the Macmahon Line was drawn.]

There is a lot of political instability in Afghanistan, and the dominance of the terrorist organisation Taliban is responsible for this. India has extended help to Afghanistan to bring peace, security and stability, to curb violence and to establish a democratic government. India is also helping Afghanistan to re-establish the communication facilities that have got destroyed due to war and to build roads. Besides this, the two countries cooperate in the fields of science and technology, and India helps Afghanistan to build schools, health facilities and irrigation projects.

India and America are two powerful nations which have democratic political systems. Right from the beginning America was India's most important trading partner, and many Indians went to America for education or work; because of the presence of these non-resident Indians, the cultural, social and economic relations between the two countries went on increasing. After the end of the Cold War the military relations between India and America increased on a large scale, and after India accepted the free market economy the speed of her economic progress slowly increased, which further strengthened trade relations between the two countries. When India conducted nuclear tests in 1998 there was tension in the relations between them, but many rounds of discussions took place after that, and through these talks America came to believe that India would use its nuclear weapons with responsibility, which completely transformed Indo-American relations. The Civil Nuclear Agreement, signed in 2005 and approved by the U.S. Congress in 2008, was an important landmark in Indo-American relations. In the last five years, cordial relations of cooperation in different areas have developed between India and America.

The clearest example the chapter gives is Afghanistan. There is a lot of political instability in Afghanistan because of the dominance of the terrorist organisation Taliban, and India has extended help to bring peace, security and stability, to curb violence and to establish a democratic government there. Along with this, India is helping Afghanistan to re-establish communication facilities destroyed by war, to build roads, and to build schools, health facilities and irrigation projects, because such development supports a stable government. A second example is Bangladesh: when the movement to liberate Bangladesh emerged out of the linguistic difference and political conflicts between West and East Pakistan, India helped Bangladesh in its freedom struggle, and Bangladesh was formed in 1971. Nepal may be mentioned as well, for the year 1990 marked the beginning of Nepal's transition to democracy; India and Nepal have been friends since the Indo-Nepalese Friendship Treaty of 1950, Nepal is dependent upon India for many of its needs, and India sent a lot of help to Nepal at the time of the 2015 earthquake.
[Note: the chapter does not state that India played any part in Nepal's transition to democracy in 1990, and it credits the establishment of democracy in Myanmar to Aung Sang Su Kyi's long drawn struggle against the military regime there, not to India.]

SAARC, the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, is a regional organisation established by the South Asian countries in 1985. The aim of this organisation is to encourage economic cooperation between the South Asian nations and thereby achieve the development of the South Asian region. SAARC is a platform on which the South Asian countries come together and discuss their common questions and interests, such as the alleviation of poverty, the development of agriculture and technological revolution. Some treaties were signed on the SAARC platform to make it easy for the South Asian countries to trade with each other, and as a part of this it has been decided that South Asia should be made into a free trade area. For an equitable development of the South Asian nations, a treaty about forming the South Asian Free Trade Area was signed and the South Asian University was established.
